analysis.investment_thesis: Landmark Global is a tiny INR 51.8 Cr micro-cap immigration consultancy with a dangerously low ROE of 0.21%, meaning the P/E of 5.25 is optically cheap but masks near-zero earning power. Immigration consulting is a fragmented, regulatory-sensitive niche without the structural India tailwinds I back — this is not a compounding story.
key_strengths: Promoter holding healthy at 72.44%, showing skin in the game
Asset-light consultancy model with low capital needs
Headline P/E of 5.25x looks optically inexpensive
key_risks: ROE of just 0.21% — business is barely earning its cost of capital
Micro-cap at INR 51.8 Cr with nil FII and only 3.37% DII — no institutional validation
Immigration consultancy is fragmented, cyclical, and vulnerable to foreign visa-policy shifts
red_flags: ROE of 0.21% is effectively a rounding error — suggests either earnings are collapsing or the P/E denominator is one-off
Low P/E combined with near-zero ROE usually signals a value trap
Opaque small-cap with minimal disclosure and no institutional coverage
analysis.detailed_analysis:
Bhai, the numbers here don't add up to an investable story. A 5.25x P/E with a 0.21% ROE tells me earnings are either non-recurring, depressed, or the capital base is bloated — none of which is the setup I want. Great Indian compounders earn 20%+ on equity; this one earns less than a savings account. At INR 51.8 Cr market cap, this is a promoter-controlled micro-cap with zero FII and just 3.37% DII participation — meaning no serious institutional money has validated this name.

The sector itself — immigration consultancy — is not where I'd bet the India growth story. It's fragmented, depends on foreign immigration policy (Canada, UK, Australia tightening rules), and has no moat. Contrast this with financial services, quality retail, or pharma where I can see 10-15 year runways. Promoter holding of 72.44% is the one positive, but good promoter alone doesn't make a great business. I'd avoid until we see multi-year ROE expansion to 15%+ and revenue growth visibility. Cheap on P/E without earning power is a classic value trap — pass.
